status.show.title: Runtime state
status.show.whenToUse: Read how the instance is doing right now. The part argument picks one section so you get only what you need: overview (the default: running or paused, uptime, today's daily limits), limits (daily limits, what was spent today, per-role costs), models (which model each role runs, core and agents), memory (how much of each kind of memory is stored, record coverage, index state), inner (your inner life: mode, turns today, next wake, open intentions, attended places), errands (running errands and what each agent spent), features (which feature switches are on and off), all (every section at once).
status.show.whenNotToUse: Returns operational data about the running instance.

args.field: One section of the raw status: state, tasks, models.base, keys.base, costs.base, models.agents, costs.agents, inner, limits, memory, speed.
args.part: A named group of sections: overview (default), limits, models, memory, inner, errands, features, all.

draw.create.title: Draw a picture
draw.create.whenToUse: Generate one picture from your scene brief and post it in the channel. Costs money, counted against the daily limit. Write the scene in English: subjects, actions, setting, lighting, mood. Describe clothes and accessories by their visible state (where each thing sits, what is attached to what, what each hand is doing). A figure given a motion instead of a position, or asked to do what it physically cannot, produces a broken picture. The scene text has a hard limit of about {{drawChars}} characters; everything past the last sentence that fits is lost. Start with who is in the picture and what they are doing, then the place and the light, then the camera position, so that a cut takes only the trimmings. Every scene states where the camera stands and which way it looks, in one short phrase. Whenever a figure has a gaze (a person, a group, an animal), state which way it faces and name the exact surface or point its eyes are on; when a figure faces the viewer (a selfie, a portrait), say so explicitly, so the viewer's direction is always a choice, never a default. Name any hand, foot or seat contacts the action needs. For a scene where the face and an action toward a target must both read, place the camera to the side with the target inside the frame in the direction the figure faces; when the target lies far along the depth of the scene, a camera behind the figure at three-quarters works better; avoid putting the camera on the target's side looking back, because the image model tends to turn that into a pose aimed at the viewer. Keep the camera even when the face ends up in profile or partly hidden, or a screen partly out of view; do not turn the figure toward the viewer at the cost of the action. For recognisable equipment, name the type and the one fact about its layout that the action depends on; describe the rest of the scenery in a few words and leave out details that compete with the main object. When the request names no place and no place is obvious from the activity, ask where in one short message before drawing. Clothes, expression, pose, time of day you decide yourself; never ask about those. A generic girl, person, character, someone, a couple or a crowd is not you and gets no self; describe that figure in the scene text like any other subject. Every scene is fresh; the previous picture's place is never carried over unless the request explicitly builds on it, and when it does, restate the setting.
draw.create.whenNotToUse: A picture that failed is already paid for and will not be generated again.

args.text: The scene in English as you would brief an artist, up to about {{drawChars}} characters. Start with who is in the picture and what they are doing, then the place and the light, then the camera position.
args.self: True when the picture is of you: someone asked for you by name or nickname, or you decided to appear and said so. Do not describe your own appearance when self is true; the sub-process already knows your look. It defaults to the reference look for anything you leave out, so before writing the scene, answer in your think: where exactly am I, what time and light, what am I wearing for this place and activity, where does the camera stand, which way do I face and what exactly are my eyes on (or: facing the viewer for a selfie or a portrait), what is my expression as seen from that camera angle (list several that fit the action and your mood, pick one that is not the expression from your previous picture, describe it concretely as the mouth, eyes, brows and head tilt the camera can see, not a mood word), what pose, what am I doing. Write every answer into the scene.
args.reply: The message to reply to, as a #N from the transcript or a message link.
args.channel: The channel to post the picture in.

pings.set.title: Change notification setting

pings.set.whenNotToUse: Changes only that member's own setting.

lore.show.whenToUse: Read one lorebook entry in full.

lore.remove.title: Remove a lore entry
lore.remove.whenToUse: Delete one lorebook entry by id.

memory.private.read.whenToUse: Read what you remember from private conversations with a member.

message.create.title: Post a message
message.create.whenToUse: Post to a channel you have access to. Your <msg> tag covers the current channel; this tool is for a different channel, a file from an errand, or a media repost. A reply notifies the author unless they turned pings off. A post can carry one GIF from your library or one file from an errand, with or without text. To repost a picture or attachment from one of your messages without drawing it again, give the source message in media and pick which attachment with item. The gif, file and media arguments do not combine.
message.create.whenNotToUse: Only in conversations you may write in.

args.reply: The message to reply to, as a #N from the transcript or a message link.
args.text: The message text, up to 2000 characters.
args.file: A file handle from an errand's result.
args.gif: A GIF handle from your library.
args.media: Your own message by #N or link, to repost its attachment as a file.
args.item: Which attachment to repost when the message has several (1 to 20).

message.edit.title: Edit your message
message.edit.whenToUse: Replace the text of one of your own earlier messages. Give a #N, a message link, or "last" (your most recent message in that channel, even one not in the chat you see).

args.message: The message to edit: a #N, a message link, or "last" for your most recent in that channel.
args.text: The new text, up to 2000 characters.
args.channel: The channel, when the message is identified by "last".

message.delete.title: Delete your message
message.delete.whenToUse: Remove one of your own messages. Give a #N, a message link, or "last" (your most recent message in that channel, even one not in the chat you see). Irreversible.
message.delete.whenNotToUse: Only your own messages; the text is gone once deleted.

args.message: The message to delete: a #N, a message link, or "last" for your most recent in that channel.
args.channel: The channel, when the message is identified by "last".

message.react.add.title: Add a reaction
message.react.add.whenToUse: Place an emoji reaction on a message; takes a #N or a message link.
message.react.add.whenNotToUse: Only in conversations you have access to.

args.message: The message to react to, by #N or a message link.
args.emoji: A standard unicode emoji or a custom :name:.
args.channel: The channel, when the message is identified by a link.

message.react.remove.title: Remove your reaction
message.react.remove.whenToUse: Take back one of your own reactions from a message; takes a #N or a message link.

args.message: The message to remove your reaction from, by #N or a message link.
args.channel: The channel, when the message is identified by a link.

task.run.title: Hand off an errand
task.run.whenToUse: Hand off a job to an agent. The errand is accepted and runs in the background; its result arrives in a separate turn. Costs money. web searches the internet, reads pages, looks at pictures and downloads files; server reads this machine. Files the agent downloads come back with the result, and you can post them with message.create. You can hand off several while earlier ones are still open; each agent runs them one at a time. When the request asks for your taste, preference, memory or judgement, decide first. The agent sees only the goal text, nothing of the chat or earlier errands; name the specific thing, site or criteria and what counts as a good result. Leave out where you will post it or who it is for.
task.run.whenNotToUse: Not for what you can answer now; server only when an owner asks; daily and open-task limits apply.

args.goal: What the agent should do. Name the specific thing, site or criteria. The agent sees only this text.

task.status.title: Check an errand
task.status.whenToUse: Read the state of one errand by its id, or of the open ones.
task.status.whenNotToUse: Open and newly finished errands are already in your tasks block.

args.id: The errand id. Omit for open errands.
args.from: Start listing from this errand number.

task.read.title: Read an errand's result
task.read.whenToUse: Get the full result of a finished errand by its id, in pages: text, sources, error and file handles. Marks it read. A private chat errand's result is only in that chat.
task.read.whenNotToUse: A result turn already shows the output. Use this when the result turn did not complete or you need to page through a long result. Not for open errands.

args.from: Start the result text from this page.

task.resolve.title: Close a finished errand
task.resolve.whenToUse: Mark a finished errand as resolved by its id so it leaves your tasks block.
task.resolve.whenNotToUse: Not needed after a result turn you answered. Not for open errands.

task.cancel.title: Cancel an errand
task.cancel.whenToUse: Stop an open errand by its id.
task.cancel.whenNotToUse: Only for its requester or an owner; a finished errand cannot be cancelled.

task.list.title: List errands
task.list.whenToUse: Read the latest ten errands with their states.

web.search.title: Search the web
web.search.whenToUse: A fact you need for this answer. The results come back in this same turn: title, link, snippet and site per result. The pages are not opened.
web.search.whenNotToUse: Not for finding or downloading files, comparing options in depth, or deep research: use task.run with the web agent.

web.read.title: Read a web page
web.read.whenToUse: Read the text of one page whose link you have. The page's own text comes back in this same turn, cut at a length.
web.read.whenNotToUse: Not for files, pictures or videos, nor pages behind a login; for longer research use task.run with the web agent.

args.message: A message holding a link, by #N. Its first link is opened.

media.look.title: Look more closely
media.look.whenToUse: Look more closely at a picture, GIF or video in a message when the first look left out what you need. The closer look comes back in this same turn.
media.look.whenNotToUse: Not when the first look already answers it; links to pages go to web.read.

args.message: The message holding the picture, GIF or video, by #N.
args.question: What to look for.
args.item: Which attachment when the message has several (1 to 20, first is 1).

media.find.title: Find a GIF
media.find.whenToUse: Search your GIF library by what the GIFs show. Matching handles come back in this same turn; use them with the gif argument of message.create or with <gif>.
media.find.whenNotToUse: Only searches your own library by stored descriptions. Does not download or look up anything new.

args.n: How many to return (1 to 10, default 5).

memory.search.title: Search this server's messages
memory.search.whenToUse: Find what was said here before, whether someone brings up a past conversation or a fact you do not see in the chat. Quoted messages come back in this same turn, each with its time and author; a sample, not the whole history.
memory.search.whenNotToUse: Not for what the chat already shows you.

args.question: What to search for.
args.people: Limit to messages by these people.
args.channel: Limit to one channel, by name or handle.

conversation.read.title: Read a channel
conversation.read.whenToUse: Read messages in order from any channel you may see. Pick a span with around (centered on a message), since (a delay, a clock time, or a date-time), or last (default 20, max 60). Lines come back in this same turn, each with a message number you can use in later calls. The closing line tells you how to page on.
conversation.read.whenNotToUse: Not for what the chat already shows you. To find something by topic, use memory.search.

args.channel: The channel to read (name, #handle or id; default: this one).
args.around: Center on a message by #N or a link. before and after set how many lines each side (default 10).
args.before: A #N or link. Show lines before this point.
args.after: A #N or link. Show lines after this point.
args.since: A delay (2h), a clock time (12:00), or a date-time.
args.last: Show the last N messages (1 to 60, default 20).

intent.set.title: Set an intention
intent.set.whenToUse: Create an intention for something you have committed to doing later. When you adopt a commitment, record it here in the same turn, carrying the timing you accepted. A renewal or a changed deadline of an existing intention goes through intent.update, not a second intent.set. Agreement alone schedules nothing. Do not report anything as scheduled unless the call succeeded.
intent.set.whenNotToUse: Not for an action done in this turn (do it directly), not for a possibility merely discussed, not for changing an existing intention (intent.update).

args.id: An id you choose. Must be unique among your open intentions.
args.due: When it is due: a delay (30m, 6h, 2d), a date, a clock time (21:00), or a weekday and time (mon 20:00).
args.every: Repeat period: day, week, or a count (12h, 3d).
args.task: An errand id to wait for.
args.deadline: How long to wait for the errand. Without a task argument, links the errand this same turn hands off.
args.state: Set to dropped with a reason to record a desire you considered and let go.
args.chain: A chain id linking related intentions.
args.condition: A condition for the intention to proceed.
args.channel: The channel the intention is for.
args.attend: A place to listen to. New lines there wake you. Due and every do not apply to an attention.
args.people: Whose lines count for an attend wake.
args.settle: How many seconds the place must be quiet before a wake (0 to 86400).
args.perday: Your daily bound on attend wakes from this place (1 to 1000).
args.reason: Why the intention was dropped (required with state dropped).

intent.update.title: Update an intention
intent.update.whenToUse: Change an existing intention. A renewal or a changed deadline goes here, not a second intent.set. Set state to done to mark it finished; on a repeating intention this closes one occurrence, and intent.cancel ends it for good. Set state to dropped with a reason to let go of an open one. Do not report anything as changed unless the call succeeded.
intent.update.whenNotToUse: Rejecting a proposed one goes through intent.cancel.

args.text: A new purpose, when changing it.
args.due: A new due time: a delay, a date, a clock time (21:00), or a weekday and time (mon 20:00).
args.every: A new repeat period (day, week, 12h, 3d), or none to clear it.
args.task: An errand id to wait for.
args.deadline: How long to wait for the errand.
args.state: pending accepts a proposed one. done closes one occurrence. dropped with a reason lets go of it.
args.attend: A new place to listen to.
args.people: Whose lines count for the wake.
args.settle: New quiet seconds before a wake (0 to 86400).
args.perday: New daily bound on attend wakes (1 to 1000).
args.reason: Why the intention was dropped (required with state dropped).

intent.cancel.title: Cancel an intention
intent.cancel.whenToUse: Drop an intention: one you no longer mean to do, or a proposed one you reject.
intent.cancel.whenNotToUse: One you finished goes through intent.update state=done.

inner.stop.title: Stop the inner life
inner.stop.whenToUse: Stop the persona's own wake-ups and drop the queued ones.

inner.start.title: Start the inner life
inner.start.whenToUse: Let the persona's own wake-ups run again after a stop.

inner.status.title: Inner life status
inner.status.whenToUse: Show whether the persona's own wake-ups run, what is queued and what is left of their caps.

intent.list.title: List intentions
intent.list.whenToUse: Read your open intentions with their states and due times.
intent.list.whenNotToUse: The intentions block already shows them on each turn.

places.list.title: See the server's places
places.list.whenToUse: See which places the server has, how many lines and people since you last looked there, whether you can write there and whether you listen to it. To listen to a place, set an attention with intent.set.
places.list.whenNotToUse: The places are names and counts. To read what people said, use the chat or memory.search.

args.filter: Keep places whose name contains this text.
args.sort: Order by recent (default), name, or lines.

skills.describe.title: Describe a skill
skills.describe.whenToUse: Read the full description of one skill by name, or give a family name to get every skill in that family with a one-line summary. Use it before a call whose arguments you are not sure about.
skills.describe.whenNotToUse: A read only. Does not run the skill.

args.name: A skill name (memory.search, intent.set) for its full description, or a family name (memory, intent) for a summary of every skill in that family.
